about:
Videobolt is an online video making platform that helps businesses promote and grow their brand through stunning videos, produced in an intuitive editor.

About us: Videobolt is an online video making platform aimed at businesses of all sizes. We empower tens of thousands of customers to promote and grow their business through stunning on-brand videos created in an intuitive online editor. In 2016, Momčilo Stojković, Uglješa Stojanović and Igor Halilović founded Videobolt with the goal of combining their knowledge of visual effects, coding and product design to create an accessible way of producing high-end videos and permanently lower the barrier to enter the video market.

Mission: We want to give everyone the freedom to make videos which make them proud.
Brand idea: Saving the world from mediocre video.
Credibility: co-founders' background in VFX and technology (the founder led special effects teams on films like Pirates of the Caribbean: Dead Men Tell No Tales and X-Men: Apocalypse), a growing global community of 100+ first-class design experts, 1,000,000+ registered users, 5,000,000+ video exports.
Core values: Simplicity (informal, practical, complexity is the greatest foe), Love for tech, Sharing (joy in seeing others grow), Friendship and community, Passion for video (never settles for average).
voice:
Personality: "That cool creative childhood friend you admire who is always willing to share his knowledge and takes pride in your success." 60% Creator (authentic, innovative, shares experience, skills and knowledge selflessly) and 40% Guy next door (non-pretentious, relatable, wholesome, genuine, down to earth).

Our passion is video and knowing how to make a video that stands out from the crowd, so everyone feels proud of what they made. The voice stays constant. The tone adapts to context, audience, medium and situation.

Voice:
- Friendly: approachable, plainspoken, empathetic. Direct but never rude. Easy to start a conversation with.
- Confident: experts in video production. Authority comes from expertise, not pretension. We respect the expertise of other people and brands.
- Encouraging: everyone can accomplish great things and we help them do it. We love praise and back opinions with clear arguments. Make new things look familiar, and familiar things look new.
- A bit quirky: we don't take ourselves too seriously. Dry humor. Weird but not inappropriate. Winking, not shouting.

We are NEVER: arrogant, disrespectful, intimidating, overly official, overly familiar, patronizing, or dull.

Guiding philosophy: Empower (inform and encourage people to make the most of the platform). Guide (a friendly, helpful tour guide). Respect (put yourself in their shoes, don't patronize, they have other things to do, communicate with people rather than market at them). Speak truth (no dramatic storytelling or grandiose claims, focus on real strengths). Educate (tell readers what they need to know, not just what we want to say; don't over-explain).

Content must be clear (simple words and sentences), useful (what purpose does this serve, who reads it, what do they need), friendly (write like you're talking to a real person, warm and human, break a rule if it makes writing more relatable), and appropriate (adapt tone to who you're writing to).

Basics: lead with the main point. Be concise (short words and sentences, no unnecessary modifiers). Be specific (cut the fluff). Write positively: explain how something can be done rather than what can't be done. Use active voice.
use:
Name: Videobolt (capital V, lowercase b). Use "we" for the company and its people, "Videobolt" for the product. Never "it". To avoid repetition, call it a "platform".
Contractions are great.

Standard spellings: computer-generated (CG), double-click, dialog box, drop-down (noun/adj), drop down (verb), email, emoji (singular and plural), geolocation, homepage, high quality, high-definition (HD), login (noun/adj), log in (verb), license, lyric video(s), motion graphics, nonprofit, OK, pop-up (noun/adj), pop up (verb), signup (noun/adj), sign up (verb), SMEs (international), SMBs (North America), third party (noun), third-party (adj), tweet, retweet, username, URL, video maker, video making, visualize, visualizer, website, WiFi.
Resolutions: 720p HD, 1080p HD, 4K UHD.

Use with caution, only in marketing education with room to define them: buyer journey, conversion, customer lifecycle, integrated marketing, lead generation, marketing funnel, multichannel marketing, omnichannel marketing, product-market fit, value proposition.

Placeholder copy for template showcases: tagline "Your tagline. Your brand."; text fields named Text 01, Text 02, Text 03 in order of appearance (or write a mock narrative in our voice).
avoid:
funnel, incentivize, leverage, disruption, disruptor, thought leader, learnings, best-in-breed, and other fluffy corporate terms
Silicon Valley cliches like "rise and grind"
crushing it, killing it
ninja, rockstar, wizard, unicorn (unless literal)
internets, interwebs, or any other variation of "internet"
young, old, elderly, or any word describing a person's age
crazy, insane, or similar words to describe people
activation (for our presence at an event)
blacklist, whitelist, grandfathered, slave, master, deaf, blind, and any other racist or ableist terms
"Videobolt's" (rewrite so it's just Videobolt)
Abbreviating or splitting the name: VB, VBolt, VDBLT, "Video bolt"
Calling Videobolt an app, website or tool
"Click here" or "Click for more information"
Asking for retweets, likes or favorites
Irrelevant trending hashtags
Textspeak like "4" for "for" or "u" for "you"
Dramatic storytelling and grandiose claims
mechanics:
American English (Merriam-Webster). AP Stylebook for anything not covered here.

Capitalization: sentence case for headings, subheadings, buttons, checkboxes, form fields and email subject lines. Title case for page titles, form titles and main navigation. Never capitalize random words mid-sentence. Emails and URLs in lowercase. Capitalize team and department names but not the word "team" (Marketing team).

Numbers: spell out one to nine and numbers starting a sentence, numerals from 10. Commas from 1,000. Write numbers under a million in full (150,000), use 150k only when space is tight. Millions and billions: 6 million videos, $3.2 billion; in headlines 6M, $3.2B. Use % (not "percent"). Spell out fractions (two-thirds). Ranges with a hyphen and no spaces (20-30 days); use from/to across units (from 30 minutes to 2 hours).
Dates: Saturday, January 24 (abbreviate Jan. 24 if short on space). Time: 7 am, 7:30 pm, 7 am-10:30 pm, 5-9 pm, noon, midnight. Default time zone CET. Decades: the 80s, the 90s (no apostrophe), early 2010s.
Money: €10, €15.99, $19.99; spell out "euro" in lowercase without the sign. "$7.99 per video", not "$7.99/video".

Punctuation:
- Serial (Oxford) comma in lists.
- Em dash (—) for asides, no spaces in body text; with spaces in titles and headers. Never commas for an aside. Hyphen with no spaces to join words (first-time user).
- No semicolons. Use an em dash or a new sentence.
- Exclamation points sparingly, never more than one, never in failure messages or alerts.
- No ellipses for drama, in titles, or instead of "etc."
- No ampersands except in brand names (allowed in tweets and buttons).
- Periods and commas inside quotation marks. Single quotes for quotes within quotes.
- Don't use quotes for Videobolt products, features or UI elements.
- Possessives: Chris's, users'.

Formatting: italics for titles of long works and for Videobolt website or editor elements (click Produce & Download). Bold for emphasis, sparingly. No underline, no combining bold, italic, caps and underline. One space between sentences.
Lists: numbered only when order matters. If one item is a full sentence, punctuate all items; otherwise no end punctuation, capitalize the first word.
Abbreviations: spell out on first use unless widely known (API, HTML). File types in caps (GIF, PDF, JPGs).
People: full name on first mention, then first name. Keep diacritics (Momčilo, Uglješa). Singular "they" when gender is unknown. Never "one" as a pronoun. Quotes in present tense ("…," says Jamie Smith). Capitalize a job title only for a specific role.
Other companies: use their own spelling (iPad, YouTube, Yahoo!) and refer to them as "it".
Jargon: plain English. Briefly define any technical term (e.g. rendering).

Emoji: support, use judgment; email, no more than one per paragraph; website, with serious consideration; blog, none.
audiences:
People who understand the power of video but don't have the skills, time or budget needed to handle quality video making. Our platform lets them create high-quality videos on the go by customizing templates made by design experts, so they can manage video production independently at an affordable price.

Businesses of all sizes, especially small and medium-sized businesses (SMEs internationally, SMBs in North America), who want to promote and grow their brand with on-brand videos.

Write for both people who read every word and people who skim: group related ideas and use descriptive headers.
pillars:
Types of content we post on social: product news, brand marketing, external art, design comparisons, product guides, industry news, curios.

Themes from our core values: simplicity (complexity is the enemy), love for tech, sharing knowledge, friendship and community, passion for video and never settling for average.
ctas:
Make the next step clear. Lead with the verb the reader will do: Read the full blog, Create your video, Subscribe.
Buttons: always a verb, a clear expectation of what happens, sentence case, no exclamation marks (Log in, Sign up, Edit, Upload). Ampersands are OK in buttons.
Links: link the relevant keywords, never "click here". Don't link articles (a, the, our) or trailing punctuation.
Never ask for retweets, likes or favorites. Tag the subject of a post when appropriate.
Email: from "Videobolt" or "Videobolt team"; subject lines in sentence case, under 9 words or 60 characters, tell don't sell, at most one | spacer; preheader expands the subject line.
platforms:
Instagram is our lead channel. We make content for Instagram first and repost it elsewhere. Video always takes priority over static images, and our formats take priority over what the networks suggest in the feed. Placeholders like profile, cover and carousel images use the network's recommended sizes.

Formats: 16:9 landscape (primary), 1:1 square, 9:16 vertical, 4:5 post. Keep the same principles, such as margins, across every format of the same piece.
- Instagram: 4:5 for feed video and images. 9:16 for Stories and Reels. In ads, 9:16 for Stories and 4:5 for the feed. Keep captions under 2-3 short paragraphs. An emoji is fine.
- Facebook: 16:9 or 1:1 (16:9 first if the original is 16:9). 2-3 short paragraphs.
- LinkedIn: 16:9 or 1:1 (16:9 first).
- Twitter/X: video in 1:1, images in 16:9. 280 characters.
- YouTube: 16:9 video. Custom 16:9 thumbnails for our own educational videos only (templates and mashups just use a frame from the video).

Performance advertising is video only.
Write short but smart: simplify the idea rather than altering spelling. "info" is fine, "4" for "for" is not.
Hashtags are deliberate, to promote an event or group content. Never irrelevant trending ones.

lookColors.name: VB White
lookColors.usage: The primary, most recognizable colour. Simplicity and minimal design. Use as empty space so the composition can breathe. The VB white theme is the primary theme.

lookColors.name: VB Black
lookColors.usage: Logo colour and text. Clarity and strong contrast against white. Base of the secondary VB black theme.

lookColors.name: VB Teal
lookColors.usage: Primary accent, the modern successor of the original blue. Highlights elements. Use only one accent colour per composition.

lookColors.name: VB Violet (Magenta)
lookColors.usage: Strong accent. Together with teal it creates the high-tech, sci-fi neon look that runs through Videobolt. Blog uses #EB00C1.

lookColors.name: VB White 2
lookColors.usage: White spectrum surface for panels and boxes in the white theme.

lookColors.name: VB White 4
lookColors.usage: 1px borders on boxes in the white theme.

lookColors.name: VB White 8
lookColors.usage: Darkest step of the white spectrum: secondary text and accents in the white theme. White spectrum: 1 #FAFBFC, 2 #F6F7F9, 3 #EDEEF3, 4 #DDDFE8, 5 #D1D4E0, 6 #C3C8D9, 7 #7F86A3, 8 #2A314F.

lookColors.name: VB Black 3
lookColors.usage: Black spectrum surfaces for the VB black theme and accents in VB elements. Black spectrum: 1 #C5C5C5, 2 #979797, 3 #242529, 4 #1F2023, 5 #121212.

lookColors.name: VB Green
lookColors.usage: Functional colour. Can be a blog accent.

lookColors.name: VB Blue
lookColors.usage: Functional colour for active selection. Last resort for branding.

lookColors.name: VB Indigo
lookColors.usage: Blog only, as the dominant note of hero-image gradients.

lookType.style: Black, always all caps, e.g. 208px with 80% line height
lookType.usage: Main brand typeface for display: titles, headings and branding elements at large sizes. Black weight for big standalone headlines and as background text in VB elements.

lookType.style: Bold for headlines with body text (e.g. 58px, 100% line height); Regular for subheads (e.g. 38px, 110%)
lookType.usage: Bold heads paired with body text. Regular as subhead or short body inside VB elements. Ads must use Sinter in Black and Regular.

lookType.style: Regular and Bold; 18px and below, 130% line height
lookType.usage: Secondary brand font for functional and body text at small sizes. Job ads: Sinter Bold heads, Roboto Regular body.
Only for the videobolt.net lockup (VB symbol + videobolt.net), small and in corners.

lookLogo:
The VB logo is the primary branding and is always preferred over the symbol. Never modify, distort or redesign it.
Colours: monochrome only. Positive (VB Black logo on a light background) is the primary logo. Negative is white on a dark background. Always keep enough contrast. A mild, tasteful gradient on the logo is allowed. Never two colours (symbol in one, text in another).
Clear space: X = the letter "O" rotated 90° and duplicated. The symbol's clear space is X/2.
Minimum size: logo length at least 2× the margin.
Placement: the logo works centered or aligned to edges and corners.
VB symbol: secondary, only where the logo or the name is already prominent (e.g. the end of a presentation or a social post). Never standalone out of context. Never in corners. Never above text. Never with any font that isn't part of the logo. When centered, nudge it slightly right so it reads as optically centered.
videobolt.net lockup (symbol + videobolt.net in Sinter Demi): only where a link can't be added (e.g. a last slide), small, in corners, never as a central element. Logo extend: logo + a 16:9 rounded rectangle holding an extension like .net or BLOG.
Email: black logo on white in the header, readable but not oversized.
lookText:
Margins: at least 4% of the longest side of the largest composition (16:9). Mandatory on standalone pieces.
Safe zones (keep important text and messages out): Stories, about 250px (~13%) top and bottom, leaving a 74% safe area. Reels, about 220px (~11%) top and 420px (~22%) bottom, leaving about 69%.
Hierarchy: Sinter Black caps for big standalone titles, Sinter Bold for heads, Sinter Regular or Roboto for supporting text. Avoid columns that are too narrow or too wide.
Never shrink text until it's unreadable at social sizes.
YouTube thumbnails: as few words as possible, positioned as the main focus. White text with a black outline, one of the rare places we use outlines.
Subtitles (current team practice): all caps, punctuation stripped except apostrophes and question marks.
lookCamera:
Photos: the human side is dominant. People actively working, at the computer, in the process of creating. Several people engaged in a creative activity that suggests using Videobolt. Technology as our domain. Mood: mystery, a job well done, neon palette, synthwave feel.
Avoid overly staged, suggestive stock photos (generic presentation, handshake deal, posed team, "made a cool video" clichés).
YouTube thumbnails: a person explaining the content (or doing the related action) in the foreground right after the text, with a shadow in a VB secondary colour as an accent. Never too small compared to the text.
lookGraphics:
VB rectangle: rounded-corner rectangles are a signature element, in 16:9 whenever possible. Radius scales with size (e.g. 7px, 12px, 20px). Not too sharp and not too round.
VB elements: a background layer, usually big Sinter Black caps text in a visibly milder colour that sets the general context, plus a foreground headline and subhead that define the topic. The back layer is always softer than the front.
Icons: optional, from Font Awesome Solid. Don't overdo them.
Depth: subtle drop shadows only, to lift fields off white backgrounds. 1px borders on boxes. Mild gradients.
Composition: use the golden ratio wherever possible, measured from the largest element. Use only one accent colour per composition.
Themes: VB white (primary) uses the white spectrum. VB black (secondary) uses the black spectrum.
Blog hero: a 16:9 VB rectangle. Hook on the left, subject on the right, CTA and colour coding in the bottom quarter. Text slightly overlaps the subject without hurting readability. Gradients from the VB palette (teal, indigo, magenta, green, blue), always light to dark or dark to light.
Thumbnail backgrounds: visuals from VB templates (e.g. a visualizer for a music video), or a calm abstract background if readability suffers.
lookDos:
Default to the VB white theme, with plenty of white space.
Keep the logo monochrome and high contrast.
Use VB rectangles with rounded corners and 16:9 proportions.
One accent colour per composition, usually VB Teal.
Respect margins (4% minimum) and social safe zones.
Pair teal with magenta when going for the neon, high-tech look.
Put video first. Choose video over static whenever possible.
lookDonts:
Modify, distort, recolour in two colours, or redesign the logo.
Put the VB symbol in corners, above text, or next to any other font.
Use strong drop shadows with harsh contrast.
Use busy, confusing backgrounds or gradient fade-outs on hero images.
Change the order of gradient colours or use colour combinations outside the VB palette.
Shrink the subject smaller than the hook on blog heroes or thumbnails.
Use more than one accent colour in a composition.
Place key text or messages inside Story or Reels safe zones.
